release_steps.name: installed ORM and shared initialization/Doctor context
installed Google SDK protocol and PostgreSQL lifecycle
installed OpenBao TLS outage and PostgreSQL lifecycle
installed shared configuration on genuine fresh recovery
installed keyword public-slot genuine fresh recovery

boundary: One mapped UPDATE RETURNING with explicit typed record and tenant equality (or declared fixed scope), one physical-column-key assignment dictionary and synchronize_session=False. Direct columns/tuples/scalars/entities retain native values, labels, identity state, NULL/coercion/constraint/savepoint behavior. Current RETURNING roots/shape, immutable request and exact new frames bind the driver and protected outputs. Native sync/async/SQLModel, current-value removal and real AppRole/OpenBao custody are exercised.
failures_retained: Initial two native-oracle cases passed without protection and reproduced protected refusal.
Source 1 and 2 found optional native AST members assumed present on UPDATE; corrected grammar reads preserve typed refusal.
Source 3 found native ORM annotations returning ciphertext bytes. Fresh annotated clones now select the owned authenticated reader without changing labels or caller statements.
Source 4 refused separately generated native projection bind identities. Exact compiled projection constants are now independently captured and checked at the driver.
Source 6 had two incorrect missing-row coercion expectations; source 7 captures actual native SQLSTATE and aborted transaction behavior and passes.
Source 8 caught a changed RETURNING list concealed by a memoized native column list. Current roots and entity/column shape are now revalidated; source 9 passes 79 new/shared controls.

Source 10 used mapped attribute assignment keys in a native single-statement dictionary and passed SQLModel params positionally. Source 11 establishes native physical keys/keyword params and reproduces protected alias refusal. Source 12 passes the corrected sync/async/SQLModel renamed-label removal journey.

Source 13 passes 273 combined regressions. Source 14 adds signed-int64 and multiple-protected-output evidence and passes 67 new cases. Prior installed release 1 passes but predates the next counterexample.

Source 15 reproduces two cases accepting a missing row identity for an unchanged protected output. DML RETURNING now requires a real record even for NULL; SELECT outer-join NULL behavior remains separate.

Source 16 selects nonexistent test filenames and runs no tests. The corrected full affected inventory in final source 17 verifies the new refusal plus shared INSERT RETURNING, SELECT outer joins, DML, provider and fork regressions.
limits: Bounded PostgreSQL16/psycopg/SQLAlchemy/SQLModel cell. Embedded values(), arbitrary filters, unprotected-table UPDATE, Core, alias/expression/label RETURNING, identity/tenant assignment, automatic/fetch synchronization and executemany RETURNING are not admitted by this route.

Unchanged protected outputs have SELECT context authentication, not new-frame/freshness proof. Public outputs have no cryptographic integrity claim. Hostile database completeness/freshness is not established.
Result authentication or key expiry can fail after SQL execution; the caller must roll back. Existing stale identity objects under synchronize_session=False retain native behavior until refresh.
The signed-int64/multiple-protected-output test uses the existing empty-schema adapter fixture; UUID scoped/fixed and native provider journeys use product protection/removal.

One UPDATE per logical operation is observed; this is not a latency/throughput qualification. Existing six latency failures and all full production gates remain UNKNOWN or failed at their recorded boundaries.
Full prior hosted CI is b01d66599456583520ed3a0b73822907c07ec70d; this boundary binds local source and installed wheel until a later hosted run is verified.
